crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is a core method in qualitative analysis for identifying, analyzing, and reporting patterns, or themes, within textual data such as interview transcripts, open-ended survey responses, and field notes.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation covers the conversion of recorded interviews into written text and the labelling of who spoke when.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding patterns in lived experience is a qualitative and mixed methods research activity.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis is the work of drawing together findings from two or more ethnographic or closely observational studies into a single comparative account.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data, often called mixed methods, is the practice of bringing narrative, observational, or interview material together with counts, measurements, or statistical summaries in one study.

sections.body: Qualitative analysis and mixed methods is the part of AI research that deals with words, talk, images, field notes and other unstructured material. Artificial intelligence is now used to transcribe interviews, separate speakers, suggest codes, group similar passages, find recurring themes and summarize ethnographic material. These systems often rely on speech recognition, natural language processing, clustering and large language models. The aim is not to replace the researcher's judgment but to speed up repetitive work and make large text collections easier to inspect. Mixed methods adds a further step, linking coded themes to numbers such as survey scores or counts. The work is practical, and it sits close to the messy reality of human accounts.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Transcription of clear audio is largely solved, but speaker separation remains difficult when people talk over each other, use strong accents or rely on specialist vocabulary. Thematic coding can be assisted by AI, yet the hard parts are context, irony, silence and the reasons behind a code. Pattern finding in lived experience can surface clusters and topics, but it can also flatten difference and miss meaning that only appears in a single account. Ethnographic synthesis is harder still, because field notes and observations carry tacit knowledge that summaries often lose. Combining qualitative and quantitative data is possible, but many studies still place the two strands side by side rather than truly integrate them. The honest limits include consent, privacy, bias in training data, reproducibility and the cost of checking AI output by hand.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section follow the path of a qualitative or mixed methods project. Thematic Coding is the core page for assigning labels to passages and building a codebook. Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation covers the step before coding, where audio becomes text and voices are told apart. Finding Patterns in Lived Experience looks at how themes emerge across many accounts and how AI can help without erasing the particular. Ethnographic Synthesis deals with pulling together observations, documents and field notes into a coherent account. Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data explains how coded themes can be joined to statistical results in one design, and the site's library holds 288 research papers, with each page linking to original papers rather than to a search tool.
